section: Related Work: 2.1 Variant and phenotype extraction from the biomedical literature

candidates.title: Improving automated deep phenotyping through large language models using retrieval-augmented generation
candidates.summary: RAG-HPO extracts phenotype phrases with an LLM and assigns HPO terms via retrieval; on 112 published case reports with 1,792 manually assigned terms it reached precision 0.81, recall 0.76, F1 0.78, most false positives being broader ancestor terms.
candidates.reason: LLM HPO extraction evaluated on published case reports against manual annotations rather than a held-out database; no per-value quotes or three-state status.

candidates.title: An evaluation of GPT models for phenotype concept recognition
candidates.summary: Tests gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4 for HPO concept recognition on abstract and clinical-observation corpora; best in-context setup gave document-level F1 0.58 on abstracts and 0.75 on clinical observations, with non-deterministic, run-to-run inconsistent outputs.
candidates.reason: Core evaluation of GPT models for HPO extraction on abstracts; documents run-to-run inconsistency and annotation-based scoring.

candidates.title: Enhancing phenotype recognition in clinical notes using large language models: PhenoBCBERT and PhenoGPT
candidates.summary: Develops BERT- and GPT-based phenotype recognizers for clinical notes and notes that earlier tools such as PhenoTagger do not support negation.
candidates.reason: LLM phenotype extraction on clinical notes rather than case reports; relevant to negation/absence handling.

candidates.title: High-Throughput Phenotyping of Clinical Text Using Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Applies GPT-4 to OMIM clinical summaries to identify, categorize and normalize signs to HPO; GPT-4 outperformed GPT-3.5-Turbo and approached inter-annotator concordance, with remaining weaknesses in normalization.
candidates.reason: LLM phenotype extraction scored against manual annotation on database summaries rather than full-text case reports.

candidates.title: Enhancing human phenotype ontology term extraction through synthetic case reports and embedding-based retrieval: A novel approach for improved biomedical data annotation
candidates.summary: Uses synthetic case reports and embedding-based retrieval to improve LLM-based HPO term extraction.
candidates.reason: Recent LLM HPO extraction method framed around case reports; evaluated against annotations.

candidates.title: PubMind: Literature-Based Genetic Variant Extraction and Functional Annotation Using Large Language Models
candidates.summary: LLM pipeline over abstracts and full text extracting variant-disease-pathogenicity relations into a database of about 1.3 million variants; about 10% overlapped ClinVar, with over 80% pathogenicity concordance on the overlap.
candidates.reason: LLM variant extraction from literature compared against ClinVar; closest prior to database concordance evaluation.

candidates.title: AutoPM3: enhancing variant interpretation via LLM-driven PM3 evidence extraction from scientific literature
candidates.summary: Open-source LLM system with Text2SQL table extraction and RAG to extract ACMG PM3 evidence; on PM3-Bench (1,027 ClinGen variant-publication pairs) it reached 86.1% accuracy for variant hits and 72.5% recall for in-trans variants.
candidates.reason: LLM variant extraction from full-text tables and text evaluated against ClinGen curation.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Detection of Genetic Variants in Biomedical Literature
candidates.summary: Compares four LLMs (including LLaMA 3.3, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3) for gene and variant extraction from prostate cancer literature; best 98% precision, 92% recall, but LLMs occasionally introduced unsupported information.
candidates.reason: Direct LLM variant-extraction evaluation; notes unsupported inferred content, relevant to per-value provenance.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Variant-Centric Functional Evidence Mining
candidates.summary: Retrieves literature via LitVar2 and uses LLMs to classify full-text functional evidence for variants; o4-mini reached 96% accuracy with higher specificity than gpt-4o-mini.
candidates.reason: Recent LLM evaluation on full-text variant evidence against curated labels.

candidates.title: CGBench: Benchmarking Language Model Scientific Reasoning for Clinical Genetics Research
candidates.summary: Benchmark of language models on clinical-genetics curation tasks built from expert curation, including evidence scoring and verification from literature.
candidates.reason: Benchmark of LLMs on variant/gene curation from papers scored against expert annotations.

candidates.title: Generative AI Accelerates Genotype-Phenotype Characterization of a 1600-Case Leigh Syndrome Virtual Cohort from Published Literature
candidates.summary: Gemini-2.5-pro with human-in-the-loop curation processed over 2,300 cases from published case tables, mapping raw clinical data to HPO with >90% accuracy, yielding a 1,679-case Leigh syndrome cohort.
candidates.reason: Closest analogue: LLM-built case-level genotype-phenotype cohort from published literature for a rare disease.

candidates.title: MSeqDR PMD-VR: An Expert-Curated Virtual Registry of 11,000 Mitochondrial Disease Cases Established Through Literature Mining and Generative AI Augmentation
candidates.summary: Semi-automated, LLM-assisted pipeline harmonizing about 11,000 literature-derived mitochondrial disease cases with variant pathogenicity and HPO-based data elements.
candidates.reason: Literature-derived case-level registry built with generative AI; comparison point for scale and evaluation design.

candidates.title: tmVar 3.0: an improved variant concept recognition and normalization tool
candidates.summary: Pre-LLM tool for recognizing and normalizing variant mentions in biomedical text.
candidates.reason: Standard non-LLM baseline for variant extraction/normalization from literature.

candidates.title: Tracking genetic variants in the biomedical literature using LitVar 2.0
candidates.summary: LitVar 2.0 links variants to publications across PubMed and PMC using text mining.
candidates.reason: Variant-paper linking resource; outputs links rather than per-patient records with quotes.

candidates.title: AVADA: toward automated pathogenic variant evidence retrieval directly from the full-text literature
candidates.summary: Machine-learning system that extracts variant mentions from full text and converts them to genomic coordinates; recall estimated against articles linked to ClinVar pathogenic variants.
candidates.reason: Full-text variant extraction evaluated with reference to ClinVar-linked articles; pre-LLM baseline.

section: Related Work: 2.3 Case-level rare-disease resources, imperfect reference databases, and memorization

candidates.title: ClinVar: improving access to variant interpretations and supporting evidence
candidates.summary: Describes ClinVar's aggregation of submitted variant interpretations and supporting evidence.
candidates.reason: Primary reference for ClinVar as the database used as ground truth.

candidates.title: ClinVar: updates to support classifications of both germline and somatic variants
candidates.summary: Recent ClinVar update describing classification types and submission changes.
candidates.reason: Current ClinVar description for submission categories and classification types.

candidates.title: Sources of discordance among germ-line variant classifications in ClinVar
candidates.summary: Analyzes about 74,000 ClinVar classifications; clinical laboratories show high concordance in many areas, while literature curation and research submissions, older and low-penetrance variants show more discordance.
candidates.reason: Shows ClinVar is an imperfect reference, especially for literature-curated records.

candidates.title: Clinical laboratories collaborate to resolve differences in variant interpretations submitted to ClinVar
candidates.summary: Laboratories reassessed variants with conflicting ClinVar interpretations and resolved many discordances.
candidates.reason: Evidence that ClinVar assertions conflict and change, limiting use as fixed ground truth.

candidates.title: Variant Classification Concordance using the ACMG-AMP Variant Interpretation Guidelines across Nine Genomic Implementation Research Studies
candidates.summary: Measures inter-laboratory concordance of ACMG-AMP variant classification across nine research studies.
candidates.reason: Quantifies disagreement in classification, bounding achievable concordance with a database.

candidates.title: Identification of Misclassified ClinVar Variants via Disease Population Prevalence
candidates.summary: Uses population allele frequencies and disease prevalence to flag ClinVar pathogenic variants that are likely misclassified.
candidates.reason: Shows ClinVar ground truth contains errors.

candidates.title: Evaluating variants classified as pathogenic in ClinVar in the DDD Study
candidates.summary: Examines ClinVar pathogenic variants found in the Deciphering Developmental Disorders cohort and how often they explain participants' phenotypes.
candidates.reason: Evidence on reliability of ClinVar pathogenic assertions as reference standard.

candidates.title: Major Causes of Conflicting Interpretations of Variant Pathogenicity in Rare Disease: A Systematic Analysis
candidates.summary: Reports that 5.7% of rare-disease variants in ClinVar have conflicting interpretations and analyzes biological and technical causes.
candidates.reason: Recent quantification of ClinVar conflicts in rare disease.

candidates.title: Clinical variants paired with phenotype: A rich resource for brain gene curation
candidates.summary: Brain Gene Registry pairs clinically identified variants with phenotypes and reports the proportion of variants novel to ClinVar and other databases.
candidates.reason: Evidence that ClinVar is incomplete for known disease variants (database gap).

candidates.title: The evaluation of tools used to predict the impact of missense variants is hindered by two types of circularity
candidates.summary: Shows that overlap between training data and benchmark databases inflates apparent accuracy of variant effect predictors.
candidates.reason: Classic argument for keeping reference databases out of the method being scored (circularity/leakage).

candidates.title: A corpus of GA4GH phenopackets: Case-level phenotyping for genomic diagnostics and discovery
candidates.summary: Describes phenopacket-store, a manually curated corpus of case-level GA4GH phenopackets from published case and cohort reports.
candidates.reason: Main curated case-level resource; shows manual curation coverage limits.

candidates.title: Assessing the Pathogenicity, Penetrance, and Expressivity of Putative Disease-Causing Variants in a Population Setting
candidates.summary: Genotype-first analysis in a population cohort showing lower penetrance and milder expressivity than clinically ascertained series.
candidates.reason: Evidence that phenotype-first literature overstates penetrance and phenotype frequencies relative to unselected cohorts.

candidates.title: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Detects training-data contamination in black-box LLMs by guided completion of instance prefixes and overlap scoring (ROUGE-L/BLEURT), applied to GPT-3.5/4.
candidates.reason: Black-box guided-completion memorization probe usable on closed models; basis for the probe design.

candidates.title: Data Contamination Quiz: A Tool to Detect and Estimate Contamination in Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Black-box contamination test asking the model to pick the original instance among perturbed variants.
candidates.reason: Alternative black-box memorization probe for closed models.

candidates.title: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
candidates.summary: Shows verbatim memorization grows with model size, duplication and prompt length, measured by prefix-prompted extraction.
candidates.reason: Foundational work on verbatim memorization measured by prompting, motivating memorization caveats.

candidates.title: Europe PMC in 2023
candidates.summary: Database update describing Europe PMC, which indexed over 42 million abstracts and over 9 million full-text articles by September 2023.
candidates.reason: Most recent primary Europe PMC paper (NAR database issue, PMID 37994696).

candidates.title: The state of OA: a large-scale analysis of the prevalence and impact of Open Access articles
candidates.summary: Using Unpaywall data, estimates at least 28% of the scholarly literature is open access and that OA articles receive about 18% more citations.
candidates.reason: Requested citation (Piwowar et al.; PeerJ 6:e4375, PMID 29456894); introduces the Unpaywall data used for OA lookups.

section: 3. Methodology - 3.5 Held-out ground truth, pre-registration and outcomes

candidates.title: Probable Inference, the Law of Succession, and Statistical Inference
candidates.summary: Introduces the score interval for a binomial proportion (Wilson interval).
candidates.reason: Requested citation for Wilson intervals (JASA 22(158):209-212; DOI confirmed on Crossref).

section: 3. Methodology - 3.5 Held-out ground truth, pre-registration and outcomes

candidates.title: Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
candidates.summary: Introduces the bootstrap as a general resampling method for estimating sampling distributions, relating it to the jackknife.
candidates.reason: Requested citation for the bootstrap (Ann. Statist. 7(1):1-26).

section: 4. Experiments - 4.8 O4 and O5: bias arm, memorization and the open-weight comparison

candidates.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
candidates.summary: Technical report for DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total, 13B activated parameters), mixture-of-experts models with million-token context and hybrid attention.
candidates.reason: Primary report introducing the DeepSeek-V4 family including V4-Flash; no separate V4.1 report was found (arXiv v1 dated 2026-04-26).
